title: Gas Station
description: Given gas available at each station on a circular route and the cost to travel to the next station, return the starting station index from which you can complete the circuit once, or -1 if impossible (the answer is unique if it exists).

reference.use_case: Finding a starting point on a circular route from which a vehicle can complete the full loop, when each stop adds fuel and each leg consumes some.
system_examples: Delivery and bus loop routing — choosing where a vehicle should start so it never runs out of fuel or charge
Cyclic cash-flow planning — choosing the start month of a recurring schedule so the running balance never goes negative
reference.explanation: If total gas ≥ total cost a solution exists, and one pass that resets the start whenever the running tank goes negative finds it in O(n), because no station inside a failed segment can be a valid start. The same 'running balance never below zero' reasoning applies to cyclic resource scheduling.
